title: DiscImageStudio: burn visible artwork onto CDs, DVDs and Blu-ray discs
abstract:
簡體中文 | 繁體中文 | English | 日本語 全能的光碟盤面可見影像生成與燒錄工具 Disc Image Studio 是一個多平臺的光碟盤面影像生成與燒錄工具，幫助您使用任何燒錄光碟機在任何 DVD / CD / 單層藍光 光碟上刻蝕出肉眼可見的影像。 效果預覽 概述 Disc Image Studio 可將一張圖片轉換成符合 CD、DVD 與單層 BD-R 光碟物理層約束的資料，燒錄後將使光碟盤面呈現肉眼可見的圖案。 介面預覽 快速開始 Windows 下載 win-x64.exe 後可直接執行。Linux 或 macOS 請下載與 CPU 匹配的 實驗性 CLI 壓縮包，解壓後執行 ./disc-image-studio --help 。這些釋出包均自帶 .NET 執行時。 GitHub Releases 1. 新建工程 在主頁選擇 CD、DVD 或藍光，指定輸出位置後建立工程。 2. 設計盤面 在設計頁匯入圖片，用圖層完成排版，並在右欄「影調」模組調整抖動、伽馬、亮度與灰階檔位。 3. 預覽與匯出 在預覽頁核對盤面投影，在匯出頁生成 ISO / RAW / WAV+CUE，或使用即時燒錄功能直接寫入空白碟片。 即時燒錄為實驗性功能，請只使用可報廢的測試介質。 功能 光碟資料生成 CD 支援 ：支援任何 CD 。您可匯出帶格式頭的 WAV 音軌及配套 CUE，相容 cdrecord, ImgBurn等燒錄軟體；也允許匯出 RAW 音軌。詳見 CD 燒錄相容說明 。 DVD 支援 ：支援任何 DVD。您可匯出 ISO 映象。 藍光支援 ：支援任何單層 BD-R 25 GB，支援純繪圖與 UDF 2.01 檔案。詳見 ADDING_BLURAY.md 。 隨盤檔案 ：CD／DVD／藍光可在設計頁直接選擇要儲存的資料夾及內圈／外圈位置，也可在匯出頁調整；設定隨工程儲存。 檔案區域預覽 ：混合盤的設計投影和成品讀回用黃色標出檔案區（含檔案系統）。 介質灰度方案 ：CD 與 DVD 均使用黑白二階，CD 使用 0D / AA ，DVD 擾碼域使用 A5 / 92 。詳見 PHYSICAL_MODEL_AUDIT.md 。 灰度抖動工具 ：獨立程式也可將原圖處理為 0/255 黑白二階 PNG；支援開啟或拖入原圖、並排預覽及無損 PNG 匯出。詳見 使用與構建說明 。 碟片預設 ：內建數個品牌的光碟參數，覆蓋 CD／DVD／BD。您也可將自己標定好的資料貢獻給我們，詳見 預設維護說明 。 輔助標定 Disc Image Studio 提供了一套智慧且精準的輔助標定流程，相較人工肉眼識別標定，輔助標定演算法將可確定的盤面物理資料精確度從 10 -6 提升到了 10 -14 。校準前採用恆定軌距，十字線的徑向線條出現明顯彎曲；使用輔助標定得到的三次軌距參數重新生成並燒錄後，線條更接近徑向直線。 校準前 · 恆定軌距 校準後 · 三次軌距 P20261004-133519.jpg P20261004-135416.jpg 流程與參數說明見 輔助標定說明 。 燒錄 映象檔案輸出 ：您可以匯出完整 ISO / RAW 檔案並使用合適的燒錄軟體手動燒錄。 即時流式燒錄（實驗性） ：CD、DVD 與 BD-R 邊生成邊燒錄，不儲存完整映象；BD-R 走 MMC 順序寫入。 不要使用非空白介質！ 系統與裝置要求 桌面版需要 Windows 10 2004（2004/20H1，19041）及以上，或 Windows 11。 構建：.NET 10 SDK（ global.json 鎖定 10.0.x）；自行構建的非自包含 GUI 需要 .NET 10 Windows 桌面執行時。Release EXE 已包含執行時，無需另行安裝 .NET。 “即時燒錄”功能需要一臺 Windows 可識別的 CD / DVD / BD 燒錄機與空白碟片；BD-R 需要支援順序寫入的單層空白盤。 構建與執行 dotnet build DiscImageStudio.slnx -- configuration Release
dotnet run -- project src / DiscImageStudio.App -- configuration Release 構建迴歸檢查： dotnet run -- project src / DvdImageSolver -- configuration Release -- selftest
dotnet run -- project tests / DiscImageStudio.ArchitectureTests -- configuration Release 版本規則、CI 生成 EXE、Release 草稿檢查、MSIX 打包與簽名流程見 釋出指南 。 命令列 Linux（glibc）可選 linux-x64 或 linux-arm64 。Apple Silicon Mac 選 osx-arm64 ，Intel Mac 選 osx-x64 。CLI 在本地生成映象，實際寫盤可交給支援相應映象或音軌的燒錄軟體。 使用 .NET 10 SDK 從原始碼執行 CLI dotnet run --project src/DiscImageStudio.Cli -c Release -- --help CLI 可讀取 PNG、JPEG、BMP 和 GIF，使用動畫圖片的第一幀。下面的例子用兩扇區音軌驗證安裝，同時生成配套 CUE。 ./disc-image-studio cd-generate --input picture.png --output sample.wav --sectors 2 命令 說明 solve 使用固定快速紋理對映（CW 方向）生成 DVD 映象，黑白紋理可選抖動混合 encode 將單個 DVD ECC 塊編碼為 NRZI 通道電平 calibrate 標定投影：按生成幾何從 DVD 源圖片取樣，按實測幾何投到盤面 simulate 按實測半徑對生成的 DVD ISO 做讀回模擬 selftest 執行 DVD 引擎的確定性迴歸自檢 cd-generate 無隨盤檔案時生成 WAV + CUE / RAW 音軌；指定 --data-dir 時生成 CD 資料盤 ISO cd-preview-warp 標定投影：按實測幾何投影 CD 源圖片 cd-preview-track 按標定幾何渲染已有的 WAV 或 RAW CD-DA 音軌（讀回模擬） bd-generate 生成完整 BD-R ISO，並寫出 <iso>.json sidecar bd-info / bd-probe / bd-encode 匯出 BD 參數、原始負載探針或單個 ECC 簇診斷 各命令的完整參數見對應文件。 原始碼結構 src/DiscImageStudio.Cli/ Linux 和 macOS 離線命令列入口
src/DiscImageStudio.ImageIO/ WIC 和跨平臺影像編解碼
src/DiscImageStudio.Core/ 介質無關的模組契約、工程/預設模型、任務與命令目錄
src/DiscImageStudio.Imaging/ CD/DVD/BD 共用的圖片預處理與抖動輔助

tests/ 無第三方測試框架的架構迴歸測試
packaging/ MSIX 清單與打包指令碼
tools/ 獨立輔助工具與資產生成指令碼
docs/ 架構、引擎、預設、釋出等文件 文件 文件 內容 ARCHITECTURE.md 模組抽象、層間邊界與擴展規則 LOCALIZATION.md 介面語言配置、系統語言回退與翻譯資源維護 DVD_ENGINE.md DVD NRZI 影像約束求解器的約定、編碼鏈與自檢覆蓋 CD_AUDIO_COMPATIBILITY.md CD 音軌格式、位元組序與重影排查 ADDING_BLURAY.md 藍光模組的物理模型、生成/燒錄鏈路與擴展點 DISC_PRESETS.md 可編輯碟片預設的分層 JSON 格式與合併規則 CALIBRATION.md 照片矯正（框選碟片實體最外緣與中心孔邊緣）、曲線標定與 DVD 三次軌距擬合 PHYSICAL_MODEL_AUDIT.md CD / DVD 生成物理模型複核 VALIDATION.md 各輪構建、迴歸與實盤測試的本地驗證記錄 RELEASING.md GitHub Release、MSIX 打包、簽名測試與商店提交流程 CHANGELOG.md 版本變更記錄 參考標準 Disc Image Studio 的實現與物理模型主要參考以下規範： 介質 標準與版本 本專案採用的範圍 CD-R ECMA-394，第 1 版，2010 年 12 月 — Recordable Compact Disc Systems CD-R Multi-Speed （ 官方 PDF ） CD-R 介質、多速錄製及 CD-DA 相容關係；本專案生成 CD-DA 音軌。 DVD 公共格式 / DVD-ROM ECMA-267，第 3 版，2001 年 4 月 — 120 mm DVD – Read-only disk （ 官方 PDF ） DVD 資料幀、ECC、EFMPlus 編碼及附錄 G 轉換表；可記錄盤的介質規則另參考 ECMA-359。 DVD-R ECMA-359，第 1 版，2004 年 12 月 — 80 mm (1,46 Gbytes per side) and 120 mm (4,70 Gbytes per side) DVD Recordable Disk (DVD-R) （ 官方 PDF ） 單層 DVD-R 的幾何、扇區、糾錯和編碼；標準包含單面及雙面介質，雙面不等於雙層。 BD-R ISO/IEC 30190:2021，第 3 版，2021 年 1 月 — 120 mm 單層（25.0 GB）及雙層（50.0 GB）可記錄 BD 的資訊交換與儲存規範 實驗模式採用單層 25 GB 的軌道、扇區佈局、糾錯和編碼；目前不支援雙層盤。 CD 公共編碼部分還參考了 ECMA-130，第 2 版（CD-ROM，1996） 。 燒錄與介質安全須知 Disc Image Studio 不安裝驅動或服務；“即時燒錄”功能使用了 Windows 自帶的 IMAPI2，拒絕非空白介質。 “即時燒錄”功能已有部分實盤反饋，對不同裝置、介質與燒錄入口的驗證覆蓋仍有限，屬於實驗性功能，請只使用可報廢的測試介質。燒錄中斷、斷電或生成速度不足仍可能使碟片報廢！ 實際可見效果取決於碟片、燒錄機、韌體與寫入策略。 混合資料夾會在開始燒錄前掃描目錄並固定佈局；期間原始檔大小改變會安全終止任務，已開始寫入的碟片仍可能報廢。 BD-R 順序寫入不提供備用區重對映；中斷後同一碟片通常不能繼續寫入。 隱私與安全 Disc Image Studio 不聯網、不上傳檔案、不收集遙測，詳見 隱私政策 。 發現安全問題請不要在公開 Issue 中披露，按 安全政策 使用 GitHub 私密報告。 貢獻 歡迎報告問題與提交程式碼。開發環境搭建、模組邊界規則、測試要求與 Pull Request 流程見 貢獻指南 。 許可證 專案採用 GNU GPL v3.0 or later （ GPL-3.0-or-later ）。CD 交織實現包含從 CDImage 移植並修改的程式碼，整體分發沿用相容的 GPL 授權；分發二進位制或修改版時須遵守對應原始碼等要求。第三方字型與元件遵循各自許可證，詳見 授權說明 和 第三方宣告 ；應用"關於"頁也可離線檢視完整文本。 致謝 感謝 arduinocelentano 的 CDImage 專案 ，它展示了通過生成 CD 音軌在盤面形成可見影像的方法。本專案的 CD 交織實現由其相關程式碼移植並繼續修改，CD 盤面繪圖思路也受其啟發。CDImage 原作者及貢獻者的工作為本專案提供了重要基礎。 Star History

title: Intel stock collapse worsens as $3.5T chip rout spreads
abstract:
The Intel stock collapse is getting worse — and the $3.7 trillion chip rout is spreading Jared Blikre Mon, November 2, 2026 at 2:25 PM MST 3 min read INTC ^GSPC MU SNDK STX Wall Street mostly swept up last week's tech wreckage Monday. Chip stocks kept tracking mud back through the house. About 7 in 10 S&P 500 stocks rose Monday, yet nearly every chip stock fell, and the group shed more than $400 billion in market value in a single session, by Yahoo Finance calculations. Intel ( INTC ) led the way down again. The chipmaker slid about 9% after its worst day since 1974 on Oct. 30, when a disappointing forecast knocked nearly 29% off the stock. Monday's close left Intel worth less than half of what it was when September ended. And the damage didn't stick to Intel. Micron ( MU ), Sandisk ( SNDK ), Seagate ( STX ), and Western Digital ( WDC ) — the memory and storage names that led the chip boom this year — all got clobbered, falling roughly 6% to 8%. Marvell ( MRVL ) fell even harder, a drop that came as it agreed to buy Lumentum ( LITE ) in a $115 billion deal. Nvidia ( NVDA ) held up better than most, but it's still down about 16% since Oct. 6. Intel, Marvell, AMD and the memory names led the chip rout, while Nvidia barely moved. · Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace Zoom out and the mess gets bigger. Chip and memory stocks have lost about $3.7 trillion in market value since Oct. 6, by Yahoo Finance calculations. Nvidia lost the most in dollars, but Intel's drop of nearly half is the steepest among the giants. Yahoo Finance Not everything tied to AI bled. SpaceX ( SPCX ) rose, though it's still well below where it started October. Software was mixed, apart from cybersecurity stocks like Fortinet ( FTNT ) and CrowdStrike ( CRWD ), which fell with chips. Adam Johnson, founder of the Bullseye Brief and portfolio manager of the American Ingenuity Fund, thinks last week's sell-off already priced in the worst. "The market kitchen-sinked it," Johnson told Yahoo Finance on Monday. "They discounted everything that could go wrong. And when you do that, typically that's when you see a bottom." John Chambers, founder and CEO of JC2 Ventures and Cisco's former CEO, expects the gap between winners and losers to keep widening. "There will be major train wrecks," Chambers told Yahoo Finance, also on Monday. "And rising tide does not raise all boats. I would not bet against Nvidia." Stock Trader's Almanac editor Jeff Hirsch, who coined the term " Octoberphobia ," bought the sell-off on Oct. 30. History is on his side. Chips have climbed in all eight midterm cycles since 1994, measured from the last October close through the following June, by Yahoo Finance calculations. But in 2002 and 2018, they first fell about another 11%. Next up is AMD ( AMD ), which reports third quarter results Tuesday after the bell , the same day as the midterm vote. title: SOML – A Config Format for Humans
abstract:
A config format for humans SOML is short for Sindre's Objectively Marvelous Language. SOML is a config format that is pleasant to write and easy to read. The top level needs no braces, keys need no quotes, line breaks replace commas, and comments go almost anywhere. A value's type comes from its syntax, never from its content, so the type you see is the type you get: '123' is a string and 123 is an int. Dates like 2026-09-19 , instants like 2026-09-19T14:00:00Z , and durations like 30s are real values, so nobody has to guess the unit of timeout: 30 . Paths and regexes need no escaping, and prose goes in block strings. One canonical form and a shared conformance suite mean every implementation reads your file the same way. JSON has the strictness but not the comfort: quotes, commas, and braces everywhere, and no comments. YAML has the comfort but not the clarity: - list markers, nested indentation, and types guessed from content, so country: no becomes false , and version: 3.10 is a float while version: 3.10.1 is a string. SOML gives you the comfort and the strictness, without the guessing. Warning Draft spec. Feedback welcome. name: 'api-gateway'
port: 8080 # The load balancer expects this port.
timeout: 30s
launch-date: 2027-09-19
windows-path: 'C:\Users\sindre\dev'
description: ''' Terminates TLS. Routes requests to internal services. '''
allowed-origins: [ 'https://example.com' 'https://example.org'
] The same in JSON: { "name" : " api-gateway " , "port" : 8080 , "timeout" : 30 , "launch-date" : " 2027-09-19 " , "windows-path" : " C: \\ Users \\ sindre \\ dev " , "description" : " Terminates TLS. \n Routes requests to internal services. " , "allowed-origins" : [ " https://example.com " , " https://example.org " ]
} Objectives SOML is a data format for files that people write and read. It is JSON without the noise, and with comments. It keeps JSON's tree of objects and arrays and its strictness, and adds literal strings, block strings, dates, instants, and durations. Its design rests on one rule: a value's type comes from its syntax, never from its content. '123' is a string and 123 is an int. Nothing is ever retyped by inspecting it. Why SOML Less noise than JSON, and comments. Keys need no quotes, even with dashes, a line break replaces a comma, and the top level needs no braces. Comments are allowed wherever whitespace may go. What you see is the type. A string always has quotes, and a value without quotes must be a number, a date, an instant, a duration, or a keyword, or the file has an error. So country: no is an error rather than false , and '10.20' is always a string and 10.20 is always a float (IEEE 754 binary64). Strict where JSON is vague. Duplicate keys, lone surrogates, and numbers out of range are errors, not behavior that each parser decides. An int is exact to 64 bits, and 3 and 3.0 stay different types. Pleasant to write. Literal strings, so paths and regexes need no escaping, and dedented block strings for prose. Dates, instants, and durations are values. 2026-09-19 is a calendar date, 2026-09-19T14:00:00Z is an instant, and 1h30m is a duration, so no reader has to parse a string or guess a unit. Indentation is free. Braces and line breaks give the structure, so tabs, spaces, and copy and paste never change what a file means, except inside a block string, where indentation is text. One canonical form. Equal values give equal bytes, for hashing, signing, and comparing. A separate formatter keeps your comments, member order, and the spelling of each value. Its rules are part of the spec, so every conforming formatter gives the same output for the same file. Small and tested. The grammar is one pass with no lookahead, and every implementation runs the language-neutral conformance suite of nearly 1000 cases, so every implementation reads a file the same way. Example /*
Everything SOML can express, in one document. A document may also be a top-level array.
*/ # Keys are bare. Dashes are allowed, so no key needs quotes.
name: 'soml'
launch-date: 2027-09-19
released-at: 2026-09-19T14:00:00Z
'the name': 'quotes are the escape hatch, when a key needs spaces'
404: 'and a key may begin with a digit' # Strings: '...' is literal, "..." is escaped. Use ' by default.
regex: '^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$'
windows-path: 'C:\Users\sindre\dev'
shell: 'echo "$HOME" | tr -d "\n"'
escaped: "line one\nline two\t\"quoted\"\u{1f600}" # Block strings are dedented by the closing delimiter's column.
description: ''' A block string keeps its line breaks. The leading tab of each line is stripped, because the closing delimiter sits at one tab. ''' # Numbers: int and float are different types. A float is IEEE 754 binary64.
replicas: 3
ratio: 0.75
budget: 1_000_000
mask: 0b1010_1100
permissions: 0o644
color: 0xFF8800
flags: 0x00FF
limit: infinity
floor: -infinity # Booleans and null.
drained: false
owner: null # Durations: exact, in h, m, s, ms, us, and ns.
retry-after: 1m30s # Arrays. A comma or a line break separates items.
labels: ['prod', 'eu-west', 'canary']
matrix: [[1, 2], [3, 4]]
mixed: [1, 'two', true, null] # Objects. The top-level object needs no braces.
pool: { min: 2 max: 16
} # Records in arrays. Braces are required, and that is deliberate.
maintainers: [ {name: 'Sindre Sorhus', email: 'sindresorhus@gmail.com'} {name: 'Random Person', email: 'person@example.com'}
] # Line comments, and block comments, wherever whitespace may go.
# Inline objects and one-line braced documents work too:
healthcheck: {path: '/health', interval: 10s, grace: 1.5s} Why not YAML? SOML keeps what I like about YAML: comments, no braces around the file, no commas at the ends of lines, and keys without quotes. It removes what hurts: in YAML, the content of a value decides its type. In SOML, the syntax decides, so 'no' is a string, 3.10 is a float, and 2 is an int, in every implementation. What SOML adds: Block comments with /* */ , in addition to # . Durations such as 30s and 1h30m , so timeout: 30 no longer makes the reader guess the unit. Dates such as 2026-09-19 and instants such as 2026-09-19T14:00:00Z . YAML 1.2 dropped timestamps, but many parsers still read them, so a date in YAML may or may not be a string. A canonical form, so equal values give equal bytes for hashing and signing. YAML defines one for scalars only. A formatter whose rules are part of the spec. It keeps your comments, key order, and the spelling of each value. YAML says comments are not content, so tools may drop them. Editing rules, so a tool can change one value and keep the comments and layout of the rest. Error messages that usually say what to write instead. What SOML fixes: Values change type without warning. In PyYAML (YAML 1.1), country: no is false , zip: 01234 is octal 668, and time: 22:22 is base-60 1342. YAML 1.2 fixed those, but most of the ecosystem still follows 1.1, and 1.2 still guesses: version: 3.10 is a float but version: 3.10.1 is a string, and ~ , Null , and an empty value are null. SOML strings always have quotes, so country: no and version: 3.10.1 are errors. Keys are not always strings. 1: x gives an integer key in YAML, and PyYAML reads on: x as the boolean true . SOML keys are always strings, so 404: is the key '404' . Indentation is the structure. One space too few moves a key into another object, and the file still parses, which is why YAML forbids tabs there. SOML gets its structure from braces and line breaks, so indentation only helps the reader, except in a block string, where it is text. Block strings add a newline. YAML's default | keeps a trailing \n in the value; SOML does not. Large ints lose precision. js-yaml turns id: 9007199254740993 into 9007199254740992 . A SOML int is an exact int64; a larger one is an error. Duplicate keys go unnoticed. For a: 1 then a: 2 , PyYAML keeps 2 and says nothing. The spec forbids duplicates, but after type resolution 1: and 01: may or may not collide, depending on the schema. SOML compares the decoded strings and reports each duplicate.

title: Charles Tandy, the mastermind behind Radio Shack
abstract:
Charles David Tandy was the chairman of the board, president, and chief executive officer of the Tandy Corporation. He was born May 15, 1918 and died November 4, 1978. Tandy was involved in the creation or expansion of three retail chains: Tandy Leather, Radio Shack, and Pier 1 Imports. Early life Charles Tandy was instrumental in creating three retail empires: Tandy Leather, Pier 1 Imports, and Radio Shack. Tandy was the second of three children born to Carmen (née McLain) and David Lewis Tandy in Brownsville, Texas, on May 15, 1918. Charles’ youngest brother, Bill, went on to run his own chain of leather craft stores in the early 1950s before merging with Tandy Corporation. At the age of 10, Charles and a classmate started selling scraps of leather from his father’s store to classmates for spare change, teaching them how to make belts out of them. With another classmate whose father owned a boot company, they started making heavier belts from scraps of boot leather that they sold to department stores. In 1935 Tandy graduated from Central High School in Fort Worth, Texas. Charles Tandy’s education and early career Tandy’s father co-owned the Hinckley-Tandy Leather Company with his friend Norton Hinckley. After flunking out of Rice Instutute in his freshman year, he graduated from Texas Christian Academy in 1940. While in college, he sold women’s shoes. He attended Harvard Business School but did not graduate. In the spring of 1941, the Navy offered commissions to Harvard Business School students. Tandy applied and was accepted, serving 6 years. While in the Navy he set a record for selling war bonds. In 1945, he married Gwen Johnston, a wealthy widow 14 years his senior. While he was in the Navy, he observed patients recovering in Navy hospitals doing leathercraft for therapy and recreation. He wrote a letter to his father suggesting this might be a way to expand Hinckley-Tandy’s business after World War II ended. This led to them setting up a mail order business, Tandycraft, after he left the Navy. Tandy developed his small family leather business into an international corporation. He first turned it into a leather craft company when shoe rationing in World War II almost killed the business, and later expanded into selling leather and tools to make such products as wallets. Hinckley and Tandy split in 1950, with Hinckley taking the part of the business that sold shoe findings, and Tandy taking the leathercraft business. Taking Tandy Corporation Public In 1954, David Tandy suffered a heart attack, exposing a weakness in the corporate structure. Since Tandy was a private company, his death would have forced a liquidation of the company in order to pay the inheritance taxes. They sought a way to take the company public to protect it. The company wasn’t really large enough to conduct a traditional IPO, so instead, they sought to merge with a company that was already listed on the New York Stock Exchange. After shopping around for prospects, Charles Tandy engineered a leveraged buyout of the Tandy Leather Company by the American Hide and Leather Company, based in Boston, in 1955. The Tandys and their leadership didn’t agree with the direction American Hide and Leather took the company after the merger. A power struggle ensued, resulting in the Tandys, their extended family, and Tandy managers buying as much stock in the company as they could, often using borrowed money. In 1959, they forced a proxy battle to take over the company. As a result, Tandy partisans received five of the nine seats on the board. They quickly divested three unprofitable subsidiaries American Hide and Leather had purchased after merging with Tandy, moved the corporate headquarters to New York to facilitate the divestitures, then moved operations to Fort Worth. In 1960, they changed the name to Tandy Corporation, taking the ticker symbol TAN. Pier 1 Imports By 1962, Charles Tandy had concluded he had ambitions bigger than the leather craft business could satisfy. One of the businesses they looked into was Cost Plus Imports, which sold imported furniture and other goods out of a converted warehouse at near-wholesale prices. A failed public offering left the company in a cash crunch. Charles and Gwen were already planning a vacation to San Francisco in August 1962, so they visited the store as part of the trip. They found a 15,000 square foot store, several times larger than a Tandy store, selling $7-$8 million worth of merchandise per year when a Tandy store might sell $200,000. Tandy called one of his lieutenants, Luther Henderson, to come visit the store. Tandy bought into the business, acquiring with it the right to operate stores under the Cost Plus name under Henderson’s leadership. But the partnership only lasted three years. Tandy found the business model worked well for one giant store in San Francisco, but needed substantial adjustment to work as a chain throughout the country. In 1965, they parted ways, with the Tandy-backed operation taking the name Pier 1 Imports. But Henderson and Tandy found the way Tandy operated its leathercraft stores didn’t fit the furniture business, with its longer lead times. In 1966, Tandy sold Pier 1 to Henderson for $1.8 million. Henderson and Tandy remained friendly, with Tandy even taking a seat on Pier 1’s board. Tandy chided Henderson, asking why they didn’t run the company that way when it was part of Tandy Corporation. The 1992 book Tandy’s Money Machine quoted Henderson as saying Tandy was a good mentor but he didn’t take the time to understand the differences between Pier 1’s and Tandy Leather’s business models. Given more room, Henderson thought the partnership could have worked. Radio Shack Charles Tandy saw the electronics business as a natural expansion for Tandy Corporation, another hobby with a similar business model. He approached Lafayette Electronics and Allied Electronics to no avail. So in 1961, he opened an electronics store called Electronics Crafts, soon opening a second and a third. Meanwhile, in Boston, the same bank that had helped Tandy match up with American Hide and Leather had another creditor who was having trouble meeting its obligations, an electronics store called Radio Shack . The bank had told Tandy about Radio Shack before, when he was talking with Lafayette and Allied. Tandy wasn’t able to work with Milton Deutschmann, the head of Radio Shack, but with the company $7 million in debt and losing $200,000 a month, the bank forced Deutschmann to come to the table. Deutschmann agreed to an audit, and agreed to sell for a $300,000 advance that would give Tandy the right to acquire 62 percent ownership of Radio Shack at book value. Price Waterhouse conducted an audit and concluded its book value was zero, giving Tandy control of Radio Shack for $300,000. How Charles Tandy turned around Radio Shack Tandy’s turnaround plan was to close the large stores and open a large number of smaller stores in rented locations so he could close struggling stores with minimal risk, close the catalog business, and go to cash-only sales, eliminating credit. By 1966, Radio Shack was profitable. And a decade later, it was a nationwide chain with over 3,500 company owned stores and another 3,500 franchises. This quote dates itself, but business writer Milton Moskowitz called Radio Shack “the most spectacular retail expansion under one name since the explosion of the A&P grocery chain in the early part of the century.” The subsequent disappearance of both of those chains shows how fragile business is. Maybe Charles Tandy is an Ozymandias, but at least for now there are still a fair number of people living who remember his empire. As for A&P, I had no idea it liquidated in 2015 because I live west of the Mississippi River. I remember them pulling out of Missouri in the 1970s and slowly fading away.

title: Open-Source 5G Ran Platforms: A Dual Perspective on Performance and Capabilities
abstract:
Computer Science > Networking and Internet Architecture [Submitted on 26 Aug 2026] Title: Open-Source 5G RAN Platforms: A Dual Perspective on Performance and Capabilities Authors: Maria Katarine Santana Barbosa , Iasmin Gomes , Vinícius Melo , Kelvin Lopes Dias View a PDF of the paper titled Open-Source 5G RAN Platforms: A Dual Perspective on Performance and Capabilities, by Maria Katarine Santana Barbosa and 3 other authors View PDF Abstract: Open-source implementations of the fifth generation (5G) Radio Access Network (RAN), such as OpenAirInterface (OAI) and srsRAN, have become increasingly relevant for industry and academic research, rapid prototyping, and low-cost private 5G deployments. The state of the art presents different evaluation scenarios for both platforms; however, these are often limited to individual testbed evaluations, end-to-end studies, or partial comparisons between them. In particular, there is a lack of evaluations considering different Software-Defined Radios (SDRs), RAN configurations, user applications, and numbers of real UEs. To address this gap, this paper presents a comparative evaluation of OAI and srsRAN. The study includes a qualitative assessment of supported features and deployment flexibility, followed by a quantitative performance analysis covering radio resource control setup procedures, compliance with theoretical data rates, and real application workloads with diverse quality of service requirements. Specifically, we consider Video on Demand (VoD) for data rate evaluation, Live Streaming (LS) and Cloud Gaming (CG) as latency-sensitive applications. These workloads provide a comprehensive view of each platform capability. title: The end of the end, the beginning of the end: architecture, artificial intelligence and the exhaustion of the post-classical
abstract:
This article examines how artificial intelligence (AI) is reconstituting the figure of the architect – not as an external disruption but as the latest instance of a recurring pattern in which mediating tools rewrite the discipline from within. Situating the present moment as the third in a sequence of paradigmatic “ends” diagnosed by Tafuri (1969/1973) and Eisenman (1984), the article traces a genealogy of the architect from Vitruvius through Alberti to the modern professional, and argues that generative AI has mechanically realized the post-classical project Eisenman announced as avant-garde provocation, thereby exhausting its critical force and demanding a fundamental redefinition of architectural labor.
 
 
 
 The article employs a critical-theoretical methodology combining historical genealogy with contemporary empirical evidence. It constructs a genealogy of the architect-figure organized around successive mediating instruments (orthographic projection, notation, legal seal, computation, AI), drawing on Tafuri’s ideology critique, Eisenman’s post-classical theory and Carpo’s digital-turn thesis. This theoretical framework is grounded in recent empirical data, including RIBA’s 2024–2025 AI adoption surveys, Schneider et al.’s experimental study of client-AI co-design, Bernstein’s practice-based research and World Economic Forum labor projections.
 
 
 
 The article finds that generative AI has industrialized the formal operations Eisenman theorized as avant-garde in 1984 – architecture without origin, without telos, without representational meaning – rendering the post-classical paradigm the default rather than the transgression. This exhaustion produces an asymmetric absorption: AI enters practice fastest where authorial labor concentrates (ideation, visualization) and is resisted where liability concentrates (documentation, certification), splitting the legal author from the substantive author. Five emergent functions of the architect are identified – dataset curator, question framer, output evaluator, liability bearer and system critic – collectively relocating architectural authority from form-giving to judgment.
 
 
 
 The article offers the first sustained reading of architectural AI through the combined lens of Tafuri’s ideology critique and Eisenman’s post-classical theory, demonstrating that the diffusion model mechanically performs the very operations Eisenman demanded as deliberate aesthetic transgression. This reframing moves the discourse beyond the prevailing optimism/dystopia binary toward a structural analysis of how tools historically constitute the architect-figure rather than merely assist it. By identifying five emergent functions that relocate architectural authority from authorship to judgment, the article provides a theoretically grounded framework for rethinking professional identity and disciplinary self-understanding in the age of AI.

title: Neuro-symbolic AI for proactive risk forecasting: bridging large language models and dynamic Bayesian networks
abstract:
Periodic risk reports constitute a substantial repository of operational data for project management. Despite the inherent informational value, archived records remain largely unstructured and highly fragmented. This study proposes a fully local neuro-symbolic approach for dynamic risk forecasting by translating qualitative project narratives into a quantifiable predictive engine to support decision-making.
 
 
 
 The proposed methodology adopts a mixed-methods architecture including four layers: (1) spatial morphology reconstruction using a Y-axis density clustering algorithm; (2) a hybrid pseudonymization filter; (3) a local large language model (LLM) with chain-of-thought reasoning; and (4) a symbolic causal engine powered by a dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) to quantify causal propagation into a dynamic risk index.
 
 
 
 An empirical evaluation across 28 reporting cycles spanning a 33-month large-scale infrastructure project indicates that the symbolic layer provides a temporally coherent aggregation of the output of a zero-shot perception layer operating at a macro F1-score of 53.62%. By quantifying causal risk propagation, the DBN captured a 93.59% risk-saturation state, for which the retrieved evidence identifies chronic site-clearance bottlenecks. Notably, using an alert threshold selected by sensitivity analysis together with an analytic constraint on the posterior mass attributable to the critical state (talert = 70.0%), the model outputs Bayesian probabilities alongside LLM-extracted textual evidence, yielding an anticipation interval of 1.33 reporting cycles relative to the documented administrative response.
 
 
 
 The neuro-symbolic framework bridges the gap between deep learning perception and causal inference in construction management. By coupling LLM-driven zero-shot ordinal extraction with DBN causal reasoning, the research establishes an auditable framework for risk documentation. The integrated framework transitions AI from an opaque prediction model into an accountable decision-support tool, providing stakeholders with transparent explainable AI diagnostics and supporting a shift from reactive mitigation to proactive, evidence-based risk prevention.

title: University students' disciplinary perspectives on generative AI after two years of its widespread use
abstract:
This study explores how university students use generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) across various disciplines, including STEM, Business, Education Futures, Clinical & Health Sciences (CHS), Creative and Allied Health & Human Performance (AHHP). It aims to identify discipline-based perspectives, perceived benefits, ethical boundaries and the support needs required for responsible use of GenAI tools.
 
 
 
 A survey was conducted approximately two years after the widespread use of GenAI, by which time participants were expected to be familiar with its use. Students were categorised based on their discipline, English fluency, mode of learning and level of study. Their responses were analysed to compare usage patterns, satisfaction levels and ethical considerations across disciplines.
 
 
 
 The results highlight that student perspectives on GenAI tools are discipline-dependent. STEM and Education Futures showed the highest acceptance, while CHS and Business students were more cautious and sceptical about accuracy and ethical issues. Non-native English speakers rated GenAI tools more favourably as aids for writing and comprehension. Novice users expressed enthusiasm, while expert users showed dissatisfaction due to errors and false information.
 
 
 
 The study relied on self-reported perceptions and represents a single institutional context. Broader investigations are recommended, with a particular focus on equity groups such as students with disabilities, low-SES students and remote learners.
 
 
 
 Different approaches were suggested for integrating GenAI into learning. STEM students favoured comparative tasks; CHS recommended support for diagnostic reasoning; Allied Health preferred role-playing simulations; Education Futures highlighted lesson planning; and Business students suggested case-based and productivity uses.
 
 
 
 The study provides cross-disciplinary analyses of GenAI use by students and proposes approaches for ethical and discipline-specific integration into university curricula.

title: Enabling large language models for automated compliance checking of BIM models in architectural engineering through semantic modelling and linking
abstract:
This study examines how standardised Building Information Modelling (BIM) data modelling can support large language models (LLMs) in automated compliance checking of architectural project information requirements. The focus is the Level of Information Need (LOIN) for design deliverables. The study addresses the disconnect between LLM reasoning and standardised project information.
 
 
 
 A constructive research approach is adopted to develop and evaluate an LLM-based compliance checking framework. BIM resources and LOIN-based requirements are transformed into semantic data through information modelling and linking. An Information Container for Linked Document Delivery (ICDD) organises project documents and semantic links. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects LLM interaction with graph querying, compliance checking and issue reporting services. The prototype uses data from a single architectural project. A controlled benchmark compares direct review, Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and MCP review.
 
 
 
 Direct review based on raw Turtle snippets showed limited performance because compliance evidence was often interpreted conservatively. Graph RAG achieved higher checking performance through structured graph retrieval, while MCP review achieved the best overall result by combining LLM-based task interpretation with tool-mediated checking. Performance varied across rule types. Explicit-data and derived-value rules were checked more reliably than extended data-structure rules, which were sensitive to alternative relation patterns.
 
 
 
 This study presents a prototype approach to BIM–LLM integration for compliance-oriented project information management. Project resources, information requirements and checking rules are organised through ICDD and semantic graph data. MCP-mediated interaction links requirement interpretation with executable checking services, evidence retrieval and issue reporting, enabling traceable compliance review in project delivery.

title: Business Ukrainian in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Transformation of Language Norms, Professional Etiquette, and Communicative Culture
abstract: The article develops a psycholinguistic account of how generative artificial intelligence changes professional Ukrainian-language writing, with particular attention to language norms, professional speech etiquette, communicative culture, and the educational workplace. A structured theoretical synthesis was conducted on a corpus of 29 peer-reviewed journal articles from 2022–2026. The corpus was organised into four evidence blocks: artificial intelligence in business and workplace communication; pragmatic behaviour of large language models; politeness and email communication in academic and workplace settings; and Ukrainian psycholinguistic and speech-etiquette contexts. Studies were coded for communication domain, speech act or genre, role of artificial intelligence, normative and pragmatic outcomes, relational perceptions, and contextual limitations. Because research designs and outcome measures were heterogeneous, the analysis used qualitative comparative synthesis rather than meta-analysis. The synthesis reveals three recurrent transformations. First, generative systems often strengthen formal correctness, structural coherence, and explicit politeness. Second, these gains can be accompanied by communicative conventionalisation: increased formality, formulaic organisation, reduced lexical or strategic variability, and weaker adjustment to the local interpersonal context. Third, artificial-intelligence mediation changes attributional and relational judgements: perceived authorship, authenticity, sincerity, trust, and willingness to maintain interaction may diverge from ratings of professionalism or clarity. These transformations are not uniform; their magnitude depends on communicative risk, status relations, degree of imposition, genre conventionality, source disclosure, and the extent of human revision. On this basis, a three-component model of normative optimisation, communicative conventionalisation, and attributional-relational shift is proposed. For Ukrainian professional communication, especially in higher education, generative artificial intelligence should be treated as a mediator of linguistic choice rather than a neutral editing device. The key research gap is the lack of direct empirical evidence on Ukrainian-language AI-mediated professional writing, which limits straightforward transfer of findings from English-dominant studies.
